Metro concrete fleet · rostering

H-Fleet

The daily truck board for the metro agitator fleet — replacing the HMA Metro Roster workbook with a system that knows the rules, keeps the history, and talks to the systems around it.

194 drivers 148 trucks 13 depots Working build · 8 Aug 2026

Where we started

One spreadsheet, and everything that depends on it

The metro roster runs the concrete fleet every morning. It lives in a workbook: no history, no rules, no way to see tomorrow, and one person’s copy is the source of truth.

0Days of history kept
0Licence checks
1Person who can edit
—Answer to “why was PCC2044 off?”
  • A driver with an expired heavy-vehicle licence can be rostered, and nothing objects.
  • Thursday’s shortage is discovered on Thursday morning.
  • Utilisation, breakdown patterns and leave impact can’t be measured, so they can’t be argued.

The daily board

The same board, with the rules built in

  • Drag a driver between trucks — or tap, then tap on a tablet in the yard.
  • Two dispatchers can work the same morning: every move is one transaction, so nobody can double-assign a driver, and the board re-syncs itself.
  • The Fleet doctor rail flags what needs a person: needs-cover, rostered-while-on-leave, breakdowns, expiring licences, long unbroken runs.
  • Days roll forward from each truck’s default driver; the first edit saves the whole day as reportable history.

Syncrotess

Our own allocations, read automatically

The daily allocation PDF is uploaded and matched against the real fleet — trucks by code, drivers by employee number or name. Start times and each truck’s working plant land on the board.

  • Nothing is guessed. Unknown trucks and duplicates are flagged for review before anything is applied.
  • Trucks lent to another plant for the day are marked @ plant on the board.
  • Re-importing the same sheet changes nothing — safe if two people upload it.

Risk

An expired licence stops the roster

Licences, medicals and site inductions are tracked per driver with expiry dates. A credential marked block does exactly that.

  • The system refuses the move and says why — it isn’t a warning someone can scroll past.
  • Everything else — expiring soon, medicals due — surfaces in the Fleet doctor before it becomes a roadside problem.
  • Credential types are configurable: add a ticket type, set its warning window, decide whether it blocks.

Stated plainly: the fatigue flags count consecutive days, not hours. They are a rostering guardrail — not an NHVR work/rest determination. Hours-based checking follows the telematics feed.

Planning

Thursday’s hole, visible on Monday

Cover per depot per day for the week ahead. Days nobody has touched yet are projected forward from default drivers and approved leave, so a shortage appears days before it bites.

  • Red “N short” is trucks with no driver. Click any day to open its board.
  • Public holidays and weekends are marked; leave counts sit alongside.

Drivers

The morning phone-tree, gone

Drivers open their own roster on their phone: today’s truck, start time and plant, the next two weeks, their leave and remaining balance, and their ticket expiry dates.

  • Read-only, and honest — a day that isn’t finalised is labelled provisional rather than presented as fact.
  • Leave decisions notify the driver directly.
  • Workday stays the source of truth for pay and formal leave; the screen says so.

Management

Questions the workbook could never answer

  • Which trucks keep breaking down? Ranked by the share of days spent off-road — the maintenance conversation with evidence attached.
  • Did the plan survive the morning? Rostered start times against actual departures: on-time share, average variance, and the trucks that are repeatedly late.
  • How much does the plan change? The share of truck-days that ran with someone other than the default driver.
  • Every figure is built from saved days only, and each screen states how many.

Connectivity

Built for the systems we already run

Each inbound feed sits behind one interface, chosen by configuration. Moving from a demonstration feed to the real vendor is a settings change, not a rebuild.

Integrations, working end to end

Preview first. Then apply.

  • An HR sync shows the exact changes first — new starters, field-level edits, leavers, balance updates — before anything lands.
  • Applying is repeatable: running it twice changes nothing the second time.
  • Drivers missing from a feed are reported, never deactivated — a partial extract must not stand down half the fleet.
  • Every run is recorded: what ran, by whom, and whether the data was real.

Corporate sign-in

Microsoft Entra ID with roles driven by AD groups. Deactivating someone here blocks them even with a live Microsoft account.

Depot-scoped access

A supervisor can be limited to their own depots — enforced on every write, not just hidden in the interface.

Full audit trail

Every change records who, what and when — including automated ones, and whether the source was real.

Checked on every change

Tests, type checking and a production build run automatically on each push, on two Node versions.

Boundaries held throughout: H-Fleet never computes pay or leave balances, and never writes back to Workday.
